subject: EdgeServe: JIT subprocessor onboarding & edge-cache transfer controls
messages:
From: Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@edgeserve.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial scope: edge cache transfers + JIT subprocessor onboarding

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we liked the latency controls. Before we proceed to pilot, our security team needs two things nailed down so procurement can move forward:

1) A scoped DTIA/TIA that covers edge cache nodes (US primary, EU failover) and clarifies where SCCs / UK IDTA apply when transient copies are created in the EU.
2) The process and guardrails for JIT (just-in-time) subprocessor onboarding — we occasionally enable third-party edge partners for burst caching and need assurances on notification, attestations, and limited data access.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our proposed TIA scope and sample dataflows (attachment: initial_tia_scope.xlsx - xlsx). Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can provide an editable DTIA draft and a subprocessor inventory that distinguishes persistent processors from transient edge caches?
- What evidence you can provide for SCCs / UK IDTA (SOC 2, data flow diagram, subprocessors attestation)?
- A ballpark timeline to get to a redlined draft so our procurement can schedule sign-off (target: 2-3 weeks).

We'd prefer to keep health-identifiable payloads onshore, but can accept pseudonymized payloads for caching in the EU if proper controls exist.

Appreciate a short plan and a 30-min slot this week or next to align.

Paul Meyer
Head of Security
EdgeServe

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial scope: edge cache transfers + JIT subprocessor onboarding

Paul — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answer: yes, we can. Longer answer and next steps below.

What Redwood will provide
- Editable DTIA draft (we'll send a redline for your Legal to review) (attachment: redline_dtia_draft.pdf - pdf).
- Subprocessor inventory CSV with flags for persistent vs transient and a per-region processing note (we'll provide a CSV + attestation).
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 Type II report excerpt, dataflow diagram, and a short write-up on how our edge caching works with KV/prefix caching to avoid storing PII when configured.

Key constraints and proposed guardrails for JIT edge partners
- JIT subprocessor onboarding will require: 1) attestation of controls, 2) a documented minimal-access role, 3) a 72-hr notice to customer security (or a documented exception workflow), and 4) automatic offboarding and key rotation after the burst window.
- For UK customers or where UK IDTA applies, we will map the transient cache nodes and include those as subprocessors in the UK addendum scope.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP)
- Today/Mon: Redwood sends editable DTIA + subprocessor CSV and evidence stub.
- By Wed: EdgeServe provides redlines and the Edge dataflow PDF.
- Week of Nov 2: legal alignment call (30 min).
- Week of Nov 9: final signoff target.

Availability: I'm free Tue 10/27 10:00-11:30 PT and Wed 10/28 14:00-16:00 PT. Laura (cc'd) will help coordinate track items with Operations. Kimberly, please add any legal must-haves.

Rishi
Head of Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Meyer <paul.meyer@edgeserve.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Paul / team — quick legal note before we lock the DTIA: we support the MAP Rishi proposed with a couple of additions to make the JIT path auditable and compatible with SCCs/UK IDTA expectations.

Suggested contract-level language (high level):
- JIT Subprocessor Onboarding: Redwood will provide Customer with: (i) 7 calendar days' notice prior to enabling a new transient subprocessor for production workloads or, in time-sensitive burst scenarios, a 72-hour post-enablement attestation and incident-style notification to Customer Security; (ii) proof of controls (SOC2 or equivalent) and a signed subprocessor attestation; (iii) automatic access revocation and crypto key rotation within 24 hours of session termination.
- Data Minimization for Edge Caches: Edge caches used for latency must be configurable to restrict storage of direct identifiers; where pseudonymization is used to permit EU caching, Redwood will document the pseudonymization method and provide replay mitigation controls.
- UK IDTA bucket: We'll include transient EU caches under the UK addendum scope when they receive or reconstruct EU personal data; the DTIA will include a matrix mapping cache classes to geographic legal instruments (SCC vs UK IDTA).

Operational asks for evidence handoff:
- Please attach the canonical dataflow PDF, and call out sample endpoints where health-identifiable payloads are in-scope.
- We'll produce a delta-only redline so you can see where Redwood's baseline covers the clauses and where the UK addendum mapping sits.

I'll attach a short doc with clause text templates and a checklist (attachment: kimberly_clause_suggestions.docx - docx). Rishi: can we commit to sending the inventory CSV with a per-node residency flag? That will speed EdgeServe's review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
